newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-CHRISTY MARTIN RETURNS TO TYSON CARD.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-CHRISTY MARTIN RETURNS TO TYSON CARD.

text.p: Women's professional boxing, at least in the form of Christy Martin, seems to be an idea whose time has come.

After all, if boxing can sell a heavyweight title fight with the likes of Bruce Seldon, who gave new definition to hapless and heartless when he capitulated to Tyson at 1:49 of the first round in September, why not an attractive, feminine woman who can punch and is not afraid to take a punch?

Martin, the college-educated, daughter, granddaughter and niece of West Virginia coal miners, is on the undercard of Saturday's Mike Tyson-Evander Holyfield title fight. It will be the fourth straight Tyson card she has graced.

And graced is not an over-the-top superlative, given that on the three previous Tyson dance cards -- versus Buster Mathis, Frank Bruno and Seldon -- Martin's was the best fight, some would say the only fight, of the night.

Pay-per-view executives at Showtime, the cable distributor of the card, and promoter Don King say they cannot calculate how many viewers Martin seduces. But it is suspected the chief reason they do not provide the number of "buys" they believe she brings to Tyson cards is because they do not want Martin (30-1-2) to be aware of her worth.

It seems very clear, through reported calls from fans to various local cable operators and the positive publicity she has received, that Martin, 28, has won their hearts and wallets with her bruising, technically-solid performances, tinged with more than a little femininity, which is perceived by marketers to be an important selling point for women's boxing.

Why else would King, not known for fiscal magnanimity toward fighters, be paying Martin $75,000 to put on her black eyeliner, "Hot Cinnamon" lipstick and "Warm Ginger" blush and come out like a punching Whirling Dervish in pink, firing hooks and jabs against Bethany "Foxy" Payne?

Saturday's payday for the the 5'4" (1.62 meters), 135-pound (61.2 kg) Martin, who began in a $1,000 winner-take-all Tough-Woman contest on a dare by some college friends, is her biggest in five years as a professional.
She received $15,000 for her fight on the Tyson-Mathis undercard, $50,000 on the Seldon fiasco, and now $75,000 for her scheduled six-round fight against the 15-1 Payne, who will be paid $6,000.
